condition: Superficial vein thrombosis (great saphenous vein, near the saphenofemoral junction)
summary: 58-year-old woman with varicose veins: 4 days of a painful red cord along the medial thigh; duplex shows great saphenous vein thrombus 15 cm long extending to within 2 cm of the saphenofemoral junction, deep veins clear.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Painful red cord on inner left thigh
inputs.hpi: Four days of a painful, red, hard line along the inside of the left thigh over her varicose veins, now reaching the groin crease. No fever. No leg swelling. No chest symptoms.

exam.msk: Left medial thigh: tender, firm, erythematous cord along the great saphenous vein from the knee to 3 cm below the groin crease. Varicose veins below the knee. No calf swelling or oedema.

imaging.name: Venous duplex left leg
imaging.result: Occlusive thrombus in the great saphenous vein, 15 cm long, proximal tip 2 cm from the saphenofemoral junction. Common femoral, femoral and popliteal veins compressible — no deep vein thrombosis.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Superficial vein thrombosis of left great saphenous vein within 3 cm of the saphenofemoral junction
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Superficial vein thrombosis (superficial thrombophlebitis) of the left great saphenous vein, 15 cm, extending to within 2 cm of the saphenofemoral junction; deep veins clear. Treat with therapeutic anticoagulation as for DVT.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE has no superficial vein thrombosis disease; top 3: Varicose veins, Acute cholecystitis, GORD. Symptom inference has no SVT either.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add superficial vein thrombosis (with SFJ/SPJ proximity) to PANE/symptom inference and a protocol (duplex; fondaparinux 45 days if ≥5 cm; therapeutic anticoagulation within 3 cm of the SFJ) with ICD I80.0x.

redFlags.note: Thrombus near the SFJ carries DVT/PE risk and changes treatment.
redFlags.knownGapNote: ICD I80.02 matches no pane-engine protocol and the PANE top diagnosis is below 0.20, so neither the Plan tab nor the Assessment management panel produces anything; only generic clinical prompts are shown.
redFlags.proposedFix: Add an SVT protocol with ICD I80.0x.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: ICD I80.02 matches no pane-engine protocol and the PANE top diagnosis is below 0.20, so neither the Plan tab nor the Assessment management panel produces anything; only generic clinical prompts are shown.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add an SVT protocol with ICD I80.0x.

mustInclude.note: ESVS 2021: within 3 cm of the SFJ → therapeutic anticoagulation; ≥5 cm elsewhere → fondaparinux 2.5 mg for 45 days.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: ICD I80.02 matches no pane-engine protocol and the PANE top diagnosis is below 0.20, so neither the Plan tab nor the Assessment management panel produces anything; only generic clinical prompts are shown. The varicose-veins protocol only mentions "superficial thrombophlebitis extending to SFJ" as a red flag.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add an SVT protocol with ICD I80.0x (ESVS 2021 treatment thresholds).

guideline.name: ESVS 2021 clinical practice guidelines — venous thrombosis
guideline.section: Superficial vein thrombosis: duplex ultrasound of both deep and superficial systems; SVT ≥5 cm → fondaparinux 2.5 mg daily for 45 days; SVT within 3 cm of the saphenofemoral junction → therapeutic anticoagulation as for DVT
guideline.citation: Kakkos SK, Gohel M, Baekgaard N, et al. European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2021 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Venous Thrombosis. Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2021;61:9–82.

rationale: Base superficial vein thrombosis case at the high-risk end (≥5 cm, within 3 cm of the SFJ). ESVS 2021: therapeutic anticoagulation. ICD I80.02 tests the ICD route (no protocol registered). The "rash" chip stands in for the red cord because there is no thrombophlebitis chip.
